source.method: direct line-exact text extraction of original archive source, match time and mag to preexisting 24-row immutable fixture; no raw-byte acquisition claimed

units.thermal_contrast_c: Celsius difference, tamb-tsky; qualitative proxy ONLY

moon_filter_from_separate_existing_geome: June 17 and 18 passed prior conservative Moon<-5deg position-box screen; June19 and June20 are negative controls; no new ephemeris executed
scientific_interpretation: June18 is optically brighter at all six paired timestamps and the sky-facing IR is warmer, with 2.98 C lower mean ambient-minus-sky contrast. This is consistent with greater downwelling IR from clouds/humidity, NOT a demonstrated cause. Within June18 03:50-03:55 optical brightening despite slightly cooler sky IR rejects a simplistic monotonic cloud-correction. No threshold or aerosol estimate warranted.
limitations: Posthoc selected UTC nights and retrospective analysis; not independent test
Thermal IR is a qualitative cloud proxy; unverified absolute calibration, IR FoV, emissivity, humidity and cloud type
Instrument looks at zenith 90deg; model v1 late angular support <=80deg
Unknown exact site coordinates, SG bandpass to model conversion, cloud/aerosol, artificial light and human observations
SG photometric formal errors exclude environmental and calibration bias; zero model acceptance
Moon below -5deg does not certify exactly zero lunar scatter
